history.summary: Krishna temple on Udai Mandir Road near Umaid Garden, built by the royal-household devotee Naini Bai during the reign of Maharaja Takht Singh of Marwar, hence also called Naini Bai Ka Mandir. The main shrine is of white stone on a 17-ft raised platform, surrounded by sabha mandaps with red sandstone pillars, a parikrama gallery, and shrines/statues of Shiva, Ganesha, Hanuman, Garuda, Vishnu, Surya, and a marble Nandi given by Raja Jaswant Singh in 1885. The temple is presently maintained and managed by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). FLAG: the 1869 CE/VS 1926 date comes from visitor-compiled reviews, not an official source (verify). Geocode is street-level (Udai Mandir Road), so coordinates are approximate (verify).

town_description: Jodhpur, the 'Blue City' and 'Sun City' of Rajasthan, is the historic capital of Marwar founded by Rao Jodha in 1459. Dominated by the massive Mehrangarh Fort, it is Rajasthan's second-largest city and a major tourist hub for Rajput heritage, blue-painted old-town houses, textiles, and handicrafts.

travel.railway: ~2 km from Jodhpur Junction (Udai Mandir Road / Paota side)
travel.road: On Udai Mandir Road near Umaid Garden, on the Paota to Merti Gate route; reachable by bus, taxi, or auto-rickshaw

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Janmashtami for the festive atmosphere
visitor_information.opening_hours: Summer: 6:30 AM to 7:00 AM and 6:45 PM to 7:30 PM; Winter: 6:45 AM to 7:30 AM and 6:45 PM to 7:30 PM
